questions.question: A TV news report about India shows the country's population written as 1 000 000 000 people. How should the reporter say this number out loud?
questions.explain: Group the digits in threes from the right: 1 000 000 000 has nine zeros, so it is one billion. The usual trap is saying one million, which has only six zeros and is a thousand times smaller.

questions.question: A pharmacist in Kelowna writes that a child's daily dose is four thousandths of a gram of medicine. Which number shows that dose?
questions.explain: Thousandths is the third place after the decimal point, so four thousandths is 0.004 g. Writing 0.04 g puts the 4 in the hundredths place and makes the dose ten times too big.

questions.question: A science channel says the world now has about eight billion people. Which set of digits shows eight billion?
questions.explain: A billion needs nine zeros, so eight billion is 8 000 000 000. Eight million (8 000 000) has only six zeros, which is a thousand times smaller.

questions.question: A forest study near Prince George reports that one park holds about 3 208 000 000 insects. Which digit of this number sits in the millions place?
questions.explain: Split the number into groups of three from the right, 3 / 208 / 000 / 000, so 3 is billions, 2 is hundred millions and 8 is millions. Picking the 3 mixes up the billions place with the millions place.

questions.question: A news website reports that a game has been downloaded 2 400 000 000 times. Which short form belongs in the headline?
questions.explain: Group the digits in threes: 2 400 000 000 is 2 billion and 400 million, so it is 2.4 billion. Reading it as 2.4 million shrinks the number a thousand times.

questions.question: A doctor prescribes 0.125 g of medicine for one whole day, taken in 5 equal doses. How much medicine is in one dose?
questions.explain: Divide 0.125 by 5 to get 0.025 g, or twenty-five thousandths of a gram. A common slip is 0.25 g, which is ten times too much because a zero after the decimal point was dropped.

questions.question: A photo on Ana's phone takes 4 000 000 bytes of storage and a movie takes 4 000 000 000 bytes. How many times bigger is the movie file?
questions.explain: A billion is a thousand millions, so 4 000 000 000 divided by 4 000 000 is 1 000. Count the extra zeros carefully: there are exactly three more, not two.

questions.question: A medicine bottle says each spoonful holds 250 mg of syrup. Using 1 g = 1000 mg, what is one spoonful written in grams?
questions.explain: Dividing 250 by 1000 moves each digit three places to the right, giving 0.25 g. Slipping in one extra zero gives 0.025 g, a dose ten times too small.

questions.question: A social studies page says Canada has about 40 000 000 people, while the whole world has about 8 000 000 000 people. About how many times larger is the world population?
questions.explain: Cancel seven zeros from each number: 8 000 000 000 divided by 40 000 000 becomes 800 divided by 4, which is 200. Counting one zero too few gives 20, which would mean the world had only 800 million people.

questions.question: A doctor tells a patient to take 0.75 g of medicine each day, split into 3 equal doses. Each tablet contains 0.125 g. How many tablets are in one dose?
questions.explain: First split the day's 0.75 g into 3 doses, giving 0.25 g, then 0.25 divided by 0.125 is 2 tablets. Answering 6 uses the whole day's amount instead of one single dose.

questions.question: A news app shows that a new BC hospital will cost $1 400 000 000. Four students explain what that amount means. Who is right?
options: Ana: it is $1.4 million, because a long number with zeros means millions.
Cai: it is $140 million, because one zero at the end can be dropped.
Ben: it is $1.4 billion, because the 1 stands in the billions place.
Dev: it is $14 billion, because an extra zero can be added safely.
questions.explain: Group the digits in threes from the right, 1 / 400 / 000 / 000, so the 1 sits in the billions place and the cost is $1.4 billion. Saying million instead names an amount a thousand times smaller, and zeros can never be added or dropped.

questions.question: A class tests a 250 mL sample of lake water and finds 0.006 g of salt in it. The school's tank holds 1000 times as much water as that sample. How much salt would the whole tank hold?
questions.explain: Multiplying by 1000 moves each digit three places to the left, so 0.006 g becomes 6 g. Moving only two places gives 0.6 g, which is ten times too little.
